/-!
# The low-degree game

This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
the ambient coefficient space; their conditional-linearity and distribution
invariants are recorded as proof-level obligations for later stages.

## References

The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
`def:ld-win-predicate` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`; their paper origin is
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-1010`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- Parameters for the low-degree game, including the fixed field model used by
the ambient coefficient space.  This is the Lean carrier for `def:ld-game` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-1010`.
-/
structure LdParams where
  q : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  d : ℕ
  k : ℕ
  hm : 1 ≤ m
  hd : 1 ≤ d
  hk : 1 ≤ k
  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
  hdvd : m ∣ q
  model : FixedFieldModel q

/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
field carrier in `def:ld-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := P.model.K

/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
inductive LdType where
  | point
  | aline
  | dline
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype

/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`).
-/
abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m

/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`).
-/
abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P

/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
-/
def LdSpace.point (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))

/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
-/
def LdSpace.seed (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
  z (.inl (.inr ()) )

/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
-/
def LdSpace.direction (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
  fun i => z (.inr i)

/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
-/
noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))

/-- The source uses the block quotient of the fixed integer representation.  The
`Fin.ofNat` wrapper supplies the totalized boundary behavior for the temporary
 skeleton's proof-irrelevant zero-dimension branch.  This is the projection
 clause of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
 `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
-/
def prefixProjection (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j

/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
-/
def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
  fun i => match i with
  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
  | .inr _ => 0

/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`).
-/
noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
  fun i => match i with
  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
  | .inr _ => 0

/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`).
-/
noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
  let rep := lineRepMap direction
  fun i => match i with
  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
  | .inr j => direction j

/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
-/
noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
  | .point => ldPointCL P
  | .aline => ldALineCL P
  | .dline => ldDLineCL P

/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is a named
Lean proof obligation for the prose assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`,
blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
-/
theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
  sorry

/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is the
level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
-/
theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
  sorry

/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`).
-/
abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P

/-- The finite edge set for the low-degree question graph.  Self-loops are
included so that every type has a valid endpoint pair; this is the graph in
`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
-/
def ldEdges : Finset (Sym2 LdType) :=
  (Finset.univ.image (fun t : LdType => Sym2.mk t t)) ∪
    ({Sym2.mk .point .aline, Sym2.mk .point .dline} : Finset (Sym2 LdType))

/-- The support of the typed CL question distribution, obtained by pushing a
uniform seed through the type-indexed maps.  This is the construction in
`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
-/
noncomputable def ldQuestionSupport (P : LdParams) :
    Finset (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
  (Finset.univ : Finset ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)).image (fun s =>
    ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))

/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
-/
noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
  Distribution.map
    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
    (fun s =>
      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))

/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`).
-/
inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
-/
abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))

/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`).
-/
noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
  toFun
    | .pointVals a => .inl a
    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
  invFun
    | .inl a => .pointVals a
    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
  right_inv := by
    intro x
    cases x with
    | inl a => rfl
    | inr x =>
        cases x with
        | inl a => rfl
        | inr a => rfl

instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩

noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm

/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.

## (d) Statement sketch of `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness`

```lean
/-- Soundness function of the Pauli basis test; argument order (ε, m, d, q)
everywhere, per rem:delta-qld-argument-order. Real rpow throughout. -/
noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  a * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ a *
    (ε ^ b + (q : ℝ) ^ (-b) + (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))

/-- thm:pauli (qpbt-paper 08_…tex:1426-1447): soundness of the Pauli basis test. -/
theorem pauli_soundness :
    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) [FieldModel P.q] (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
          ∃ (ιA' ιB' : Type) (_ : Fintype ιA') (_ : DecidableEq ιA')
            (_ : Fintype ιB') (_ : DecidableEq ιB')
            (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
                    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
            (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
                    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
            (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')), ‖aux‖ = 1 ∧
            -- item 1: ‖φA ⊗ φB ψ − aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}‖ ≤ δ_qld  (squared distance,
            -- via stateDistSq and deltaQld²; or state with ‖·‖ directly — either
            -- form is acceptable, document the choice)
            ‖isometryTensor φA φB S.ψ - idealState P aux‖
                ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
            -- item 2, for both players and both bases, summation over u ∈ F_q^M,
            -- w.r.t. the ideal state; O(·) constants absorbed into a (see (e)8)
            ∀ W : PauliKind,
              (∑ u : PauliRegister P,
                ‖(heteroKron
                    (conjIsometry φA ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect
                      (PauliAnswer.pauliOutcome u) ...decoded))
                    (1 : Op (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
                  - pauliProjOnA'' P W u).mulVec (idealState P aux)‖ ^ 2)
                ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
              (symmetric B-side bound)
```

Supporting definitions in Soundness.lean (all NEW, Lean-only):
`idealState P aux := reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor aux (eprState (PauliRegister P)))`;
`pauliQuestion P W : (pauliBasisTest P).QuestionA := (PauliType.pauli W, 0)` (the
`(Pauli, W)` question has content `0`, image of the 0-level CL function);
`pauliProjOnA'' P W u : Op ((ιA' × Reg) × (ιB' × Reg))` places `pauliProj W u` on the
`A''` factor, identity elsewhere (and the `B''` analogue). The A-side measurement
outcome family is the sub-family of `S.A` at outcomes `PauliAnswer.pauliOutcome u`
(other constructors carry no mass in the ideal comparison; define the family by
pattern-matching `PauliAnswer → Op` with `0` on the other constructors — this is the
faithful reading of "answer summation over `u ∈ F_q^M`").

## (e) Settled encoding decisions (do not re-derive)

1. **Polynomials — representative convention** (issue #0004, `def:polynomials-degree`):
   polynomial-valued objects are representatives, not function classes. Reuse
   `MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` where a polynomial *class* is quantified.
   Game *answers* are finite coefficient tuples exactly as printed in the paper
   ("given by its d+1 coefficients"): `Fin (d+1) → K`, resp. `Fin (m*d+1) → K`.
   Do not reuse `LDT.AxisLinePolynomial`/`DiagonalLineAnswer` (the LDT diagonal answer
   is function-encoded and `Parameters`-bundled; a bridge can come later).
   `def:ld-meas`/`PolyMeas` are NOT in this closure — do not build them now.
2. **Distributions — match LDT, not PMF**: the LDT question distributions use
   `MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution` (Finset-supported, real weights, `Error := ℝ`) with
   `IsProbability`, `avgOver`, `map`, `uniformDistribution`, `uniformOnFinset`
   (`LDT/Basic/Distribution.lean`, `DistributionUniform.lean`; product combinators in
   `DistributionProduct.lean` — verify the exact name before use). All QPBT question
   distributions are `Distribution` values; `PMF` only ever via the existing
   `DistributionPMF` bridge, never in game-facing statements.
3. **Measurements**: use `MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement`/`Submeasurement`
   (`Quantum/Measurement.lean`) as the POVM carrier; marginals and the bracket
   notation are `Measurement.postprocess` (already `\leanok` for ch12 `def:bracket`).
   Projectivity via `MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj`.
4. **States**: pure states as unit vectors of `EuclideanSpace ℂ ι` (the theorem's
   conclusion needs vector norms, isometries `→ₗᵢ[ℂ]` — reuse
   `Quantum/FiniteHilbert.lean` patterns — and `eprState`). The density-matrix
   `LDT.QuantumState` layer is NOT used in the QPBT games layer.
5. **Field model**: reuse `MIPStarRE.LDT.FieldModel q` (bundled `K ≃ Fin q`). The χ
   map (eq:chi-func) interprets `s : K` as an integer through `FieldModel.equiv`;
   the finite-field trace is the basis-independent `Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K`
   (= Tr of `Algebra.leftMulMatrix`, i.e. eq:def-trace). The self-dual normal basis
   and `def:binary-representation` are NOT in the statement closure and are deferred
   (see OPEN-6). `canonicalComplement` is defined basis-freely by the pivot
   characterization — `j` is a pivot of `W` iff restricting to coordinates `≤ j`
   increases rank — which agrees with the source's RREF construction by the
   basis-independence noted in `def:canonical-complement` (equivalence proof deferred).
6. **Qudit indexing**: the `M = 2^m` qudits and the vectors `F_q^M` are indexed by
   `Cube m := Fin m → Bool`. Never introduce `Fin (2^m)`; `M` appears only as
   `Fintype.card (Cube m)` in docstrings.
7. **Prose claims inside blueprint definitions become companion lemmas**: CL-level
   assertions ("`L_ALine` is a 2-level CL function"), uniformity of `χ(s)`,
   well-definedness remarks — each a named `sorry` lemma next to the definition, not
   a definitional obligation. Definitions themselves are direct and computable-shaped.
8. **Asymptotic `≈`/O(·) → quantitative functionals**: `def:state-distance` /
   `def:povm-distance` are encoded as explicit real error quantities (`stateDistSq`,
   `opFamilyDistSq`), mirroring how the LDT track already quantifies `≃`/`≈`
   (cf. rem:asymptotic-distance). The implicit universal constants of the blueprint's
   `≈_δ` are absorbed into the existentially quantified constant `a` of
   `pauli_soundness`; record this in the theorem docstring.
9. **Win predicates are `Bool`-valued**, answer alphabets are sum types, and
   "answers not of the prescribed form are rejected" is a predicate clause (match on
   constructor shape). Question alphabets are `Type × ambient-space` pairs — contents
   are full ambient vectors `ι → K` (images of the CL maps), not per-type refined
   types; this matches the blueprint's `(t, L_t(z))` format.
10. **`deltaQld` argument order** is `(ε, m, d, q)` with `0 < b < 1` strict and
    prefactor `a(md)^a` — per rem:delta-qld-argument-order; do not copy the classical
    `δ_ld` shape.

   164	/-- Read the low-degree register selected by a basis from an ambient Pauli

   172	  | .inl (.inl j) => pauliPointBlock W z j
   173	  | .inl (.inr _) => pauliScalarBlock z
   174	  | .inr j => pauliDirectionBlock z j

   176	/-- Embed a low-degree vector into the basis-selected Pauli blocks, clearing the
   177	other basis and the two `r` registers.  This is Lean-only coordinate plumbing
   178	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   179	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   180	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1010`.

   182	def embedLd (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   183	    (u : LdSpace P.toLdParams) : PauliSpace P :=

   185	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) =>
   186	      match W with
   187	      | .X => u (.inl (.inl j))
   188	      | .Z => 0
   189	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) =>
   190	      match W with
   191	      | .X => 0
   192	      | .Z => u (.inl (.inl j))
   193	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => u (.inl (.inr ()))
   194	  | .inl (.inl (.inr j)) => u (.inr j)
   195	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   196	  | .inr _ => 0

   206	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => 0
   207	  | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
   208	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   209	  | .inr _ => z (.inr ())

   211	/-- The source level attached to each typed Pauli CL map.  This records the
   212	exact levels in items 1--5 of `def:pauli-question-distribution`: point, line,
   213	and diagonal maps have levels 1, 2, and 3, the Pauli map has level 0, and the
   214	shared projection has level 1.  Blueprint
   215	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
   216	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1010`.
   217	-/
   218	def pauliCLLevel : PauliType → ℕ
   219	  | .point _ => 1
   220	  | .aline _ => 2
   221	  | .dline _ => 3
   222	  | .pauli _ => 0
   223	  | .pairW _ => 1
   224	  | .pair => 1
   225	  | .ms _ => 1

   227	/-- The typed CL dispatcher.  The point/line maps are the corresponding
   228	low-degree maps embedded in the selected basis block; Pair, Magic Square, and
   229	Pair/W types use the shared projection; Pauli/W is the zero-level map.  This
   230	is the direct finite-space form of `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   231	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   232	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1010`.
   233	-/
   234	noncomputable def pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   235	    PauliSpace P → PauliSpace P :=
   236	  match t with
   237	  | .point W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   238	  | .aline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   239	  | .dline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   240	  | .pauli _ => fun _ => 0
   241	  | .pairW _ => pauliSharedProjection
   242	  | .pair => pauliSharedProjection
   243	  | .ms _ => pauliSharedProjection
   244	
   245	/-- Level assertions for the typed Pauli CL maps.  These are Lean-only
   246	proof obligations corresponding to the prose following `def:pauli-question-distribution`

   248	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1010`).

   250	theorem isCondLinear_pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   251	    IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ (pauliCLLevel t) (pauliCL P t) := by
   252	  sorry

   254	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   255	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   256	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   257	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1010`.
   258	-/
   259	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   260	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   261	  let lineEdges :=
   262	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   263	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   264	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   265	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   266	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   267	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   268	  let basisEdges :=
   269	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   270	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   271	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   272	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   273	  let pairEdges :=
   274	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   275	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   276	  let msEdges' :=
   277	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   278	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   279	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   280	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   281	
   282	/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
   283	(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   284	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1010`).
   285	-/
   286	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P
   287	
   288	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   289	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   290	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   291	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   292	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1010`.
   293	-/
   294	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   295	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   296	
   297	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   298	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   299	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   300	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   301	-/
   302	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   303	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   304	  simp [pauliEdges]
   305	
   306	/-- The finite support obtained by sampling an edge and a common ambient seed,
   307	then applying the endpoint CL maps.  This is the inlined typed-CL construction
   308	of `def:pauli-question-distribution` (blueprint lines 285-329; paper
   309	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1010`).
   310	-/
   311	noncomputable def pauliQuestionSupport (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   312	    Finset (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   313	  by
   314	    classical
   315	    exact
   316	      (Finset.univ.filter fun s : (PauliType × PauliType) × PauliSpace P =>
   317	          Sym2.mk s.1.1 s.1.2 ∈ pauliEdges).image (fun s =>
   318	        ((s.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   319	
   320	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   321	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   322	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   323	-/
   324	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   325	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   326	  by
   327	    classical
   328	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   329	    exact
   330	      Distribution.map
   331	        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
   332	        (fun s =>
   333	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   334	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))
   335	
   336	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   337	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
   338	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   339	-/
   340	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   341	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   342	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   343	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   344	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   345	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   346	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   347	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   348	  deriving DecidableEq
   349	
   350	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   351	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   352	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   353	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   354	-/
   355	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   356	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   357	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   358	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   359	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   360	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   361	
   362	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   363	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   364	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   365	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   366	-/
   367	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   368	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   369	  toFun
   370	    | .value a => .inl a
   371	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   372	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   373	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   374	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   375	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   376	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   377	  invFun
   378	    | .inl a => .value a
   379	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   380	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   381	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   382	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   383	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   384	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   385	  left_inv := by
   386	    intro x
   387	    cases x <;> rfl
   388	  right_inv := by
   389	    intro x
   390	    cases x with
   391	    | inl a => rfl
   392	    | inr x =>
   393	        cases x with
   394	        | inl a => rfl
   395	        | inr x =>
   396	            cases x with
   397	            | inl a => rfl
   398	            | inr x =>
   399	                cases x with
   400	                | inl a => rfl
   401	                | inr x =>
   402	                    cases x with
   403	                    | inl a => rfl
   404	                    | inr x =>
   405	                        cases x with
   406	                        | inl a => rfl
   407	                        | inr a => rfl
   408	
   409	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=
   410	  Fintype.ofEquiv (PauliAnswerCode P) (pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm
   411	
   412	instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Inhabited (PauliAnswer P) :=
   413	  ⟨.bit 0⟩
   414	
   415	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   416	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   417	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   418	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   419	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   420	-/
   421	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   422	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   423	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   424	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   425	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   426	
   427	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   428	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   429	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   430	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   431	-/
   432	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   433	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   434	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   435	
   436	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   437	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   438	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   439	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   440	-/
   441	def validPauliAnswer (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   442	  match t, a with
   443	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   444	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   445	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   446	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   447	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   448	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   449	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   450	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   451	  | _, _ => false
   452	
   453	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   454	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   455	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   456	-/
   457	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   458	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   459	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   460	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   461	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   462	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   463	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   464	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   465	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   466	
   467	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   468	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   469	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   470	-/
   471	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   472	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   473	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   474	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   475	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   476	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   477	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   478	
   479	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   480	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   481	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   482	-/
   483	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   484	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   485	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   486	
   487	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   488	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   489	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   490	-/
   491	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   492	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   493	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   494	    (match W with
   495	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   496	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   497	
   498	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   499	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   500	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   501	-/
   502	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   503	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   504	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   505	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   506	      (a * (match W with
   507	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   508	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   509	
   510	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   511	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   512	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   513	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   514	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   515	-/
   516	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   517	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   518	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   519	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   520	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   521	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   522	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   523	
   524	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   525	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   526	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   527	-/
   528	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   529	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   530	  open Classical in
   531	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   532	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   533	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   534	      | .point W, .point W', .value u, .value v =>
   535	          decide (W = W' ∧ u = v)
   536	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   537	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u)

    27

    30	pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in

    63	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    64	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]

    90	structure Strategy (G : Game) where

    92	  ιB : Type
    93	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    94	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    95	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    96	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    97	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)

    99	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA

   108	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:1-80`.

   141	intentionally not asserted here.
   142	-/
   143	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   144	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
   145	
   146	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   186	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   187	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin

   190	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P

   192	/-- The finite edge set for the low-degree question graph.  Self-loops are
   193	included so that every type has a valid endpoint pair; this is the graph in
   194	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   195	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin

   198	def ldEdges : Finset (Sym2 LdType) :=
   199	  (Finset.univ.image (fun t : LdType => Sym2.mk t t)) ∪
   200	    ({Sym2.mk .point .aline, Sym2.mk .point .dline} : Finset (Sym2 LdType))

   202	/-- The support of the typed CL question distribution, obtained by pushing a
   203	uniform seed through the type-indexed maps.  This is the construction in

   205	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin

   209	    Finset (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   210	  (Finset.univ : Finset ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)).image (fun s =>
   211	    ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))

   214	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   215	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.

   217	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   218	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   219	  Distribution.map
   220	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   221	    (fun s =>
   222	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))

   224	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   225	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   226	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   227	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   228	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`).
   229	-/
   230	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   231	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   232	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   233	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   234	  deriving DecidableEq
   235	
   236	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   237	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   238	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   239	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   240	-/
   241	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   242	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   243	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   244	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   245	
   246	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   247	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   248	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   249	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`).
   250	-/
   251	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   252	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   253	  toFun
   254	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   255	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   256	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   257	  invFun
   258	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   259	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   260	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   261	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   262	  right_inv := by
   263	    intro x
   264	    cases x with
   265	    | inl a => rfl
   266	    | inr x =>
   267	        cases x with
   268	        | inl a => rfl
   269	        | inr a => rfl

   272	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩

   274	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   275	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm

   277	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   278	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   279	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   280	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   281	-/
   282	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   283	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   284	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   285	
   286	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   287	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   288	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   289	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   290	-/
   291	def validLdAnswer (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   292	  match t, a with
   293	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   294	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   295	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   296	  | _, _ => false
   297	
   298	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   299	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   300	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   301	-/
   302	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   303	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   304	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   305	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   306	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   307	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   308	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   309	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   310	
   311	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   312	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   313	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   314	-/
   315	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   316	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   317	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   318	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   319	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   320	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   321	
   322	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   323	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   324	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   325	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   326	-/
   327	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   328	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   329	  open Classical in
   330	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   331	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   332	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   333	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   334	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   335	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   336	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   337	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   338	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   339	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   340	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   341	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   342	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   343	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   344	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   345	      else false
   346	
   347	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   348	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   349	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-1039`.
   350	-/
   351	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   352	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   353	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   354	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   355	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   356	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   357	  μ_prob := by sorry
   358	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   359	
   360	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     5	/-!
     6	# The Magic Square game
     7	
     8	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     9	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
    10	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    11	carrier is needed here.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    25	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    27	-/
    28	inductive MsType where
    29	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    30	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    31	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    32	
    33	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    34	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    36	-/
    37	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    38	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    39	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    40	
    41	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    42	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
    43	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    44	-/
    45	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    46	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    47	
    48	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    49	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    51	-/
    52	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    53	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    54	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    55	
    56	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    57	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    58	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    59	-/
    60	inductive MsAnswer where
    61	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    62	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    63	  deriving DecidableEq
    64	
    65	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    66	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    67	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    68	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    69	-/
    70	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    71	
    72	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    73	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    74	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    76	-/
    77	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    78	  toFun
    79	    | .triple β => .inl β
    80	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    81	  invFun
    82	    | .inl β => .triple β
    83	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    84	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
    85	  right_inv := by
    86	    intro x
    87	    cases x <;> rfl
    88	
    89	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
    90	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
    91	
    92	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
    93	
    94	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
    95	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
    96	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`).
    97	-/
    98	def msWinPredicate :
    99	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   100	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   101	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   102	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   103	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   104	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   105	      decide
   106	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   107	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   108	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   109	      decide
   110	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   111	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   112	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   113	
   114	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   115	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
   117	-/
   118	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   119	  QuestionA := MsType
   120	  QuestionB := MsType
   121	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   122	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   123	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges
   124	  μ_prob := by sorry
   125	  decide := msWinPredicate
   126	
   127	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   412	instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Inhabited (PauliAnswer P) :=

   415	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   416	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   417	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   418	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   419	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   420	-/
   421	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   422	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   423	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   424	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   425	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   426	
   427	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   428	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   429	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   430	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   431	-/
   432	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   433	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   434	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   435	
   436	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   437	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   438	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   439	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   440	-/
   441	def validPauliAnswer (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   442	  match t, a with
   443	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   444	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   445	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   446	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   447	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   448	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   449	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   450	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   451	  | _, _ => false
   452	
   453	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   454	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   455	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   456	-/
   457	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   458	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   459	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   460	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   461	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   462	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   463	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   464	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   465	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   466	
   467	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   468	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   469	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   470	-/
   471	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   472	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   473	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   474	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   475	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   476	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   477	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   478	
   479	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   480	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   481	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   482	-/
   483	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   484	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   485	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   486	
   487	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   488	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   489	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   490	-/
   491	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   492	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   493	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   494	    (match W with
   495	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   496	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   497	
   498	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   499	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   500	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   501	-/
   502	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   503	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   504	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   505	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   506	      (a * (match W with
   507	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   508	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   509	
   510	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   511	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   512	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   513	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   514	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   515	-/
   516	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   517	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   518	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   519	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   520	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   521	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   522	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   523	
   524	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   525	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   526	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   527	-/
   528	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   529	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   530	  open Classical in
   531	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   532	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   533	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   534	      | .point W, .point W', .value u, .value v =>
   535	          decide (W = W' ∧ u = v)
   536	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   537	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u)
   538	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   539	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u)
   540	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   541	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u)
   542	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   543	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u)
   544	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   545	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u)
   546	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   547	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u)
   548	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   549	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   550	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   551	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   552	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   553	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β)
   554	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   555	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β)
   556	      | .ms t, .ms t', .msTriple u, .msTriple v =>
   557	          decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   558	            msWinPredicate t t' (.triple u) (.triple v))
   559	      | .ms t, .ms t', .bit u, .bit v =>
   560	          decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   561	            msWinPredicate t t' (.bit u) (.bit v))
   562	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   564	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   565	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   566	      | .aline W, .aline W', .alinePoly f, .alinePoly g => decide (W = W' ∧ f = g)
   567	      | .dline W, .dline W', .dlinePoly f, .dlinePoly g => decide (W = W' ∧ f = g)
   568	      | .pauli W, .pauli W', .pauliOutcome u, .pauliOutcome v =>
   569	          decide (W = W' ∧ u = v)
   570	      | .pairW W, .pairW W', .bit u, .bit v => decide (W = W' ∧ u = v)
   571	      | .pair, .pair, .pairBits u, .pairBits v => decide (u = v)
   572	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   573	    else false
   574	
   575	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   576	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   577	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   578	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1039`.
   579	-/
   580	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   581	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   582	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   583	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   584	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   585	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   586	  μ_prob := by sorry
   587	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   588	
   589	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   282	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   283	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   284	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   285	
   286	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   287	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   288	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   289	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   290	-/
   291	def validLdAnswer (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   292	  match t, a with
   293	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   294	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   295	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   296	  | _, _ => false
   297	
   298	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   299	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   300	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   301	-/
   302	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   303	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   304	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   305	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   306	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   307	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   308	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   309	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   310	
   311	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   312	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   313	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   314	-/
   315	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   316	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   317	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   318	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   319	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   320	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   321	
   322	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   323	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   324	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   325	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1012-1039`.
   326	-/
   327	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   328	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   329	  open Classical in
   330	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   331	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   332	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   333	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   334	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   335	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   336	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   337	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   338	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   339	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   340	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   341	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   342	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   343	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   344	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   345	      else false

   352	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   353	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   354	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   355	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   356	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   357	  μ_prob := by sorry
   358	  decide := ldWinPredicate P

     5	/-!
     6	# The Magic Square game
     7	
     8	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     9	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
    10	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    11	carrier is needed here.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    25	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    27	-/
    28	inductive MsType where
    29	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    30	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    31	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    32	
    33	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    34	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    36	-/
    37	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    38	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    39	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    40	
    41	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    42	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
    43	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    44	-/
    45	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    46	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    47	
    48	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    49	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    51	-/
    52	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    53	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    54	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    55	
    56	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    57	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    58	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    59	-/
    60	inductive MsAnswer where
    61	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    62	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    63	  deriving DecidableEq
    64	
    65	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    66	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    67	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    68	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    69	-/
    70	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    71	
    72	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    73	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    74	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    76	-/
    77	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    78	  toFun
    79	    | .triple β => .inl β
    80	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    81	  invFun
    82	    | .inl β => .triple β
    83	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    84	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
    85	  right_inv := by
    86	    intro x
    87	    cases x <;> rfl
    88	
    89	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
    90	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
    91	
    92	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
    93	
    94	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
    95	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
    96	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`).
    97	-/
    98	def msWinPredicate :
    99	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   100	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   101	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   102	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   103	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   104	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   105	      decide
   106	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   107	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   108	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   109	      decide
   110	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   111	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   112	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   113	
   114	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   115	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
   117	-/
   118	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   119	  QuestionA := MsType
   120	  QuestionB := MsType
   121	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   122	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   123	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges
   124	  μ_prob := by sorry
   125	  decide := msWinPredicate
   126	
   127	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Quantitative state and operator distances
     6	
     7	The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
     8	corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
     9	estimates to later proof stages.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	These are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:95-103`.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	/--
    26	Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
    27	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:95-103`.
    29	-/
    30	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    31	    [DecidableEq ι]
    32	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    33	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    34	
    35	private noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    36	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
    37	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm (M.mulVec ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) ψ))
    38	
    39	/--
    40	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    41	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
    42	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:95-103`.
    43	-/
    44	noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    45	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    46	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    47	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    48	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    49	    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)
    50	
    51	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   433	\subsubsection{Subfields and bases}
   434	\label{sec:subfields}
   435	Let $q$ be a prime power and $k$ an integer. 
   436	The field $\Fq$ is a subfield of $\F_{q^k}$ and $\F_{q^k}$ is a linear space of
   437	dimension $k$ over $\Fq$.
   438	Let $\{ e_i \}_{i=1}^k$ be a basis of $\F_{q^k}$ as a linear space over $\Fq$.
   439	Introduce a bijection $\downsize_q : \F_{q^k} \rightarrow \Fq^k$ between
   440	$\F_{q^k}$ and $\Fq^k$ defined with respect to the basis $\{ e_i \}_{i=1}^k$ by
   441	\begin{equation*}
   442	  \downsize_q : a \mapsto (a_i)_{i=1}^k
   443	\end{equation*}
   444	where $a = \sum_{i=1}^k a_i e_i$.
   445	This map satisfies several nice properties.
   446	First, the map is an isomorphism of $\Fq$-vector spaces: it is $\Fq$-linear and addition in $\F_{q^k}$
   447	naturally corresponds to vector addition in $\Fq^k$.
   448	Namely, for all $a,b \in \F_{q^k}$,
   449	\begin{equation*}
   450		\downsize_q (a + b) = \downsize_q(a) + \downsize_q(b)\;.
   451	\end{equation*}
   452	Second, multiplication by a field element in $\F_{q^k}$ corresponds to a linear
   453	map on $\F_{q}^k$.
   454	For all $a \in \F_{q^k}$, there exists a matrix $K_a \in \Matrix_k (\Fq)$ such
   455	that for all $b \in \F_{q^k}$,
   456	\begin{equation*}
   457		\downsize_q (a b) = K_a \, \downsize_q(b)\;.
   458	\end{equation*}
   459	The matrix $K_a$ is called the \emph{multiplication table of $a$ with respect to
   460	  basis $\{e_i\}_{i=1}^k$}.
   461	
   462	We extend the map $\downsize_q$ to vectors, matrices and sets over $\F_{q^k}$.
   463	For $v = (v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_n) \in \F_{q^k}^n$, define
   464	\begin{equation*}
   465	  \downsize_q (v) = \bigl( \downsize_q (v_i) \bigr)_{i=1}^n \in \Fq^{kn}\;.
   466	\end{equation*}
   467	Similarly, for matrix $M = (M_{i, j}) \in \Matrix_{m, n}(\F_{q^k})$, define
   468	\begin{equation*}
   469	  \downsizem_q (M) = \bigl( K_{M_{i, j}} \bigr) \in \Matrix_{mk, nk} (\Fq)\;,
   470	\end{equation*}
   471	the block matrix whose $(i,j)$-th block is the multiplication table $K_{M_{i,
   472	    j}}$ of $M_{i, j}$ with respect to basis $\{e_i\}_{i=1}^k$.
   473	For a set $S$ of vectors in $\F_{q^k}^n$, define
   474	\begin{equation*}
   475		\downsize_q(S) = \{ \downsize_q(v) : v \in S \}\;.
   476	\end{equation*}
   477	We omit the subscript and write $\downsize$ and $\downsizem$ for $\downsize_q$
   478	and $\downsizem_q$ respectively when $q$ equals to $p$, the characteristic of
   479	the field.
   480	
   481	The \emph{trace of\/ $\F_{q^k}$ over\/ $\Fq$} is defined as
   482	\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-trace}
   483	  \tr_{q^k \to q} :\; a \,\mapsto \, \Tr(K_a)
   484	\end{equation}
   485	for $a \in \F_{q^k}$, where $\Tr(K_a)$ is the trace of the multiplication table
   486	of $a$ with respect to the basis $\{e_i\}$.
   487	By definition, the trace is an $\Fq$-linear map from $\F_{q^k}$ to
   488	$\Fq$. The trace is in fact independent of the choice of basis, which
   489	can be seen from the following equivalent definition~\cite[Definition 2.1.80]{mullen2013handbook}:
   490	\[
   491		\tr_{q^k \to q}(a) = \sum_{j = 0}^{k-1} a^{q^j}\;.
   492	\]
   493	
   494	A \emph{dual basis} $\{e_1', e_2', \ldots, e_k' \}$ of $\{e_1, e_2, \ldots,
   495	e_k\}$ is a basis such that $\tr_{q^k \to q}(e^{}_i e'_j) = \delta_{i,j}$ for
   496	all $i, j \in \{1, 2, \ldots, k\}$.
   497	A \emph{self-dual basis} is one that is equal to its dual.
   498	If for some $\alpha \in \F_{q^k}$ the set $\{ \alpha^{q^j} \}_{j=0}^{k-1}$ forms a
   499	basis of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\Fq$, the basis is called a \emph{normal
   500	  basis}. Self-dual and normal bases do not exist for all fields but are guaranteed to exist under
   501	certain conditions; in particular, if $q = 2$ and $k$ is odd, as will
   502	be shown in \Cref{lem:efficient_basis}.
   503	
   504	We record some convenient facts about the maps $\downsize(\cdot)$ and
   505	$\downsizem(\cdot)$ for self-dual bases.
   506	
   507	\begin{lemma}
   508	  \label{lem:downsize_field}
   509	  Let $q$ be a prime power, $k$ an integer and $\{e_i\}$ a self-dual basis for
   510	  $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$.
   650	  This completes the proof of the lemma.
   651	\end{proof}
